title: Stockroom order and stock simulator CLI (P14 extra-large benchmark)

content.audience: Synthetic benchmark operator measuring the studio's build path at an extra-large, many-module scale
content.problem_statement: Measure whether the bounded builder, answering a round in several parts, and the independent reviewer can deliver a many-module Python standard-library CLI (a package of 11 modules with an internal API) that runs a stock and order script read from stdin: customers with discounts, items, stock lots costed first in first out, orders that are reserved or wait, allocation, shipping, cancelling and write-offs, then a text or JSON report. Judged by 25 frozen exact-output cases with held-out ones, a separate extended held-out suite and a structure check. Synthetic benchmark, not a customer product.

user_flows.name: Catalog and stock
steps: Pipe a script of ITEM and RECEIVE lines
Read each response and the report's item lines

user_flows.name: Orders and allocation
steps: Define a customer and items
Place orders
Read reserved or waiting
Receive stock and read which waiting orders become reserved
Check exit status 3 when an order still waits

user_flows.name: Shipping
steps: Ship a reserved order
Read its revenue and first-in-first-out cost
Read the report's totals line

user_flows.name: Cancelling
steps: Cancel a reserved or waiting order
Read which waiting orders become reserved

user_flows.name: Write-offs
steps: Write off available units
Read the cost removed and the item's value

user_flows.name: Prices and discounts
steps: Change a price between orders
Ship orders of a customer with a discount
Read each revenue

user_flows.name: JSON report
steps: Run with --format json
Parse the last line as JSON

user_flows.name: Script errors
steps: Pipe a script with bad lines
Read every line number and reason
Check that later lines still run and exit status 1

user_flows.name: Quiet mode
steps: Run with --quiet
Read only error lines and the report

user_flows.name: Invalid arguments
steps: Run with an argument the CLI does not accept
Read invalid input and exit status 2

scope: Python 3.8+ standard library only. Entry point src/main.py plus a package src/stockroom with __init__.py and these modules, each with a top-level function: money.py, fields.py, script.py, catalog.py, customers.py, lots.py, orders.py, commands.py, report_text.py, report_json.py and cli.py

Each of those modules is imported by main.py or by another module of the package, and main.py imports from stockroom. Each module keeps to its name: money, field rules, script lines, the catalog, customers, stock lots, orders, the commands, the two reports and the arguments
Runtime rule: QA runs python3 -I src/main.py from the product root, so src is not on the import path. main.py must insert its own directory into sys.path before importing stockroom

Arguments: --format text or json (at most once, default text) and --quiet (at most once), in any order. Any other argument, --format without text or json after it, or a repeated flag prints exactly: invalid input, then newline, and exits 2, before reading stdin

stdin is a script split into lines on newline; one trailing carriage return per line is removed. Lines are numbered from 1, counting every line. Each line is split into tokens with Python's str.split(). A line with no tokens, or whose first token starts with #, is skipped

The first token is the command, matched exactly: CUSTOMER, ITEM, PRICE, RECEIVE, ORDER, SHIP, CANCEL or WRITEOFF; anything else gives the reason unknown command. A wrong number of arguments gives bad arguments, checked before any other reason of that command

A command that fails a check changes nothing and prints line N: reason in place of its response, and the script goes on. A command reports only the first reason that applies, in the order its rule lists them. Responses and error lines are printed in script order

Fields: sku is 1 to 12 of A-Z, 0-9 or hyphen, starting with A-Z. Order id is 1 to 10 of a-z or 0-9, starting with a-z. Customer is 1 to 16 of a-z or underscore, starting with a-z. Quantity is digits with no leading zero, 1 to 100000. Percent is 0, or digits with no leading zero up to 50

Money fields (price, cost) are 1 to 7 digits with an optional . and 1 or 2 digits, no sign, kept in integer cents; a zero price is a bad price, a cost may be zero. Money is printed as optional minus sign, whole part, dot, two digits (for example -0.05, 3.10, 1200.00)

CUSTOMER name percent: reasons bad customer, bad percent, duplicate customer; response customer NAME added. ITEM sku price: reasons bad sku, bad price, duplicate item; response item SKU added. PRICE sku price: reasons bad sku, bad price, unknown item; response item SKU price P

RECEIVE sku quantity cost adds a lot of that many units at that unit cost, after the item's older lots. Reasons bad sku, bad quantity, bad cost, unknown item. Response: received SKU Q, then allocation

ORDER id customer, then 1 to 5 pairs of sku quantity (else bad arguments). Reasons bad order id, duplicate order, bad customer, unknown customer, then pair by pair from the left: bad sku, bad quantity, unknown item, repeated item (a sku already earlier in this order)

A new order records each line's current price and its customer's percent. It is reserved when every line's quantity is at most the item's available units (on hand less all reserved units), else it waits. Response: order ID reserved, or order ID waiting

Allocation, after RECEIVE and after CANCEL: waiting orders are tried in the order they were placed, and each one whose every line fits the available units at that moment is reserved and prints order ID reserved. Later orders are still tried when an earlier one still waits

SHIP id: reasons bad order id, unknown order, order not reserved. Its units leave stock from each item's oldest lots first and its reservation ends. Response: order ID shipped revenue R cost C, where C is the summed cost of the lot units taken

An order's revenue is the sum of quantity times recorded price, less the discount: that sum times the recorded percent, divided by 100 and rounded down to a whole cent. CANCEL id: reasons bad order id, unknown order, order closed (shipped or cancelled); response order ID cancelled, then allocation

WRITEOFF sku quantity removes units from the item's oldest lots first. Reasons bad sku, bad quantity, unknown item, not enough stock (quantity above the available units). Response: wrote off SKU Q cost C. With --quiet no response or allocation line prints; error lines still do

After the script the text report prints == report ==, then per item in ascending sku: item SKU price P on_hand N reserved N value V (V is the summed cost of the units left in its lots), then per order in placement order: order ID CUSTOMER STATE (reserved, waiting, shipped or cancelled)

then per customer in ascending name: customer NAME orders N shipped S spent R (orders placed, orders shipped and their summed revenue), then totals revenue R cost C profit P over shipped orders, profit being revenue less cost. --format json prints the report as stockroom-report/1 instead
Exit 1 when any line printed an error, else 3 when an order still waits after the script, else 0. No files, network, environment variables or third-party packages

data_contracts.name: stockroom/1
data_contracts.description: Synthetic command script on stdin, one command per line; responses, error lines and the report on stdout

data_contracts.name: stockroom-report/1
data_contracts.description: One line: json.dumps(report, sort_keys=True). report is {customers: [{name, orders, shipped, spent}], items: [{sku, price, on_hand, reserved, value}], orders: [{id, customer, state, revenue}], revenue, cost, profit}, in the text report's orders

data_contracts.name: stockroom-report/1 values
data_contracts.description: Money values (spent, price, value, revenue, cost, profit) are strings in the money format; orders, shipped, on_hand and reserved are integers; an order's revenue is null unless it was shipped. The == report == line is not printed

risks.risk: One builder answer cannot hold the whole program within the connection's answer cap
risks.mitigation: builder/2 answers a round in parts that are applied together; the benchmark measures that path

risks.risk: The builder imports sibling modules without fixing sys.path under python3 -I
risks.mitigation: The runtime rule is part of the frozen scope; QA would fail every case otherwise

risks.risk: A reviewer request for the whole program exceeds a small per-request input cap
risks.mitigation: Start refuses a connection whose input cap is below the benchmark's recorded floor

risks.risk: Held-out cases leak to the builder
risks.mitigation: The studio hides held-out cases; the repository copy is never sent to runtime roles

obligations: Keep this frozen version unchanged; changes need a new benchmark version
maintenance.review_interval: On recipe, role prompt, route or model change
